text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — ACME is asking for a Redwood Dedicated commit estimate for eu-west. They want ~100k tokens/s sustained with 2x burst capacity, 99.9% availability. Can we size this and call out billing implications?
Sam: Do we have their model mix / sequence lengths? that changes GPU/throughput a lot.
Maya: Mix is ~70% interactive chat (8k seq avg), 30% embeddings (short). Average response ~120 tokens. 80% of traffic during UTC 08:00–20:00.
Priya: Rough approach: convert tokens/s -> tokens/hr -> GPU-seconds. Quick ballpark calc below.
Priya: ```
# ballpark
tokens_per_s = 100000
tokens_per_hr = tokens_per_s * 3600 = 360_000_000
avg_tokens_per_infer = 120
inferences_per_hr = tokens_per_hr / avg_tokens_per_infer = 3_000_000
# if one GPU handles ~100 inferences/sec (varies by model) -> 360k inf/hr -> ~8.3 GPUs sustained
# add overhead, KV cache, and 8k contexts -> multiply by 4 -> ~34 GPUs baseline
```
Sam: That multiplier feels right for 8k context chat on A100/MI250 class workloads. embeddings are cheap but add IO.
Alex: Don't forget billing addons: reserved commit discount tiers (we model 1yr vs 3yr), egress and snapshot storage for KV caches. Those add ~5–12% on top depending on region.
Jordan: Commercially, propose phased commit: baseline 65k tokens/s committed + 35k burst credits. Reduces $/token commitment risk for ACME and lets us keep headroom.
Maya: +1 to phased approach. Need precise GPU-hour estimates for 60/80/100k sustained levels and 1.5x/2x burst to show cost delta. @Sam @Priya can you run a short sensitivity matrix and include region-specific availability notes?
Sam: On it. I'll run the perf modeler against eu-west and eu-central pools, generate GPU-hour table, and post numbers by EOD.
Priya: Note: eu-west has a shortage of reserved Mi250 capacity in July; if they want guaranteed commit we might need to place some capacity in eu-central and route via peered network. That will increase egress/latency slightly.
Alex: If we move some capacity to eu-central, I'll model cross-region pricing: egress + committed discount mismatch can add ~7% to total. Also check committed usage smoothing for month-to-month billing.
deploy-bot: capacity-sim-job-273 finished — sim results (short): 95p util=0.82 on rtx-a100-pool-3, avg p50 latency within SLO. Full report uploaded: https://redwood.internal/sim/273
Maya: Great — please include the sim link in the final deck. Also include a customer-facing commit proposal with: baseline GPUs, burst credits, failover region, expected monthly GPU-hours, and billing tiers.
Jordan: I'll draft the customer proposal language once we have the numbers — recommend 12-month commit with a 3-month phased ramp.
Sam: Dropping initial sensitivity snapshot here (short):
- 60k sustained -> ~20 GPUs baseline -> ~14k GPU-hrs/mo
- 80k sustained -> ~27 GPUs baseline -> ~20k GPU-hrs/mo
- 100k sustained -> ~34 GPUs baseline -> ~25k GPU-hrs/mo
burst 2x -> peak add ~50% transient capacity for ~20% of hours.
Priya: I'll run a more conservative model (higher context mem & NVLink overhead) and post tomorrow morning.
Alex: I'll prepare three billing scenarios (12m commit, 12m commit + burst credits, 3m ramp) and show per-token effective price.
Maya: Thanks all. Let's reconvene Tue 10am. Action items: Sam/ Priya = numbers + sim details, Alex = billing scenarios, Jordan = proposal draft. :thumbsup:
